## 1. Sector Overview

Vietnam's power system has an estimated total installed capacity of approximately 78 GW.

**Policy framework.** The National Power Development Plan VIII (PDP8), approved by Decision 500/QĐ-TTg (15 May 2023), caps coal at 30.2 GW by 2030 and mandates full coal phase-out by 2050.

content.text: Under PDP8, Vietnam will domestically generate 20% of its electricity needs with coal by 2030, increasing coal to a peak of 30 GW and replacing outstanding coal projects with LNG or renewables.

Decision 262/QĐ-TTg (1 April 2024) approved the PDP8 Implementation Plan. On 15 April 2025, Decision 768 approved the Amended PDP8, raising LNG capacity to 22,524 MW by 2030. On 30 May 2025, MOIT issued Decision 1509/QĐ-BCT with the amended implementation schedule.

**Key actors.** EVN and its generation subsidiaries (EVNGENCO1, EVNGENCO2, EVNGENCO3) own most domestic coal and gas plants.

content.text: EVNGENCO3 was established under Decision 3025/QĐ-BCT on 1 June 2012, reorganising the Phú Mỹ Thermal Power Company and receiving state capital ownership rights at several power generation companies.

PetroVietnam (PVN) and its subsidiary PV Power operate the Cà Mau, Nhơn Trạch, Sông Hậu 1, and Thái Bình 2 plants. TKV (Vinacomin) operates mine-mouth coal plants. BOT-format plants by foreign investors (Sumitomo, Marubeni/KEPCO, AES, Janakuasa, CSEC, Jaks Resources) are progressively reverting to EVN as contracts expire —

, and

content.text: EVNGENCO3 took over management, operation, repair, and maintenance of Phú Mỹ 2.2 on 4 February 2025.

**Challenges.** The LNG transition faces PPA/GSA bottlenecks; of 13 PDP8 LNG projects (~22,400 MW), only Nhơn Trạch 3&4 have reached commissioning. Coal retirements are slow. The JETP ($15.5 bn) creates political pressure for an accelerated phase-down.

## 2. Major Asset Narratives

### 2.1 Vĩnh Tân Complex (Bình Thuận)
Four coal units totalling 4,244 MW.
